page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i3g.2xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM, providing 4.0 GB of memory per core, and includes 479 GB of bundled local SSD storage. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps under a KVM hypervisor.

Benchmark evaluations indicate average multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 7006.17 and a Passmark CPU score of 8286.39. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by a stress-ng single-core score of 1314.6 and a weak single-threaded gzip compression rate. Memory bandwidth is average, reaching 50.63 GB/sec for large block read-only operations. Database operations and static web serving throughput perform in the average tier, though Redis SET operations are weak at 6.88 million operations per second. Large language model inference is limited, with poor performance on 7B parameter models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the inclusion of dedicated Intel Xeon cores and 479 GB of local SSD storage provides a balanced resource density for general-purpose workloads without requiring separate storage attachments. The server is suited for moderate database operations, static web serving, software compilation, and general-purpose applications that benefit from dedicated CPU allocation and local SSD storage, while it is less optimal for single-thread intensive tasks or heavy LLM inference.

It is configured with 32.0 GB of RAM and includes 479 GB of bundled local SSD storage, operating under a KVM hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps. Performance benchmarks place this instance in the average tier for multi-core processing, memory bandwidth, and static web serving, though single-core execution and Redis operations are relatively weak. The server offers a balanced hardware profile, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring dedicated CPU resources and local storage. It is best suited for general-purpose applications, moderate database operations, and static web serving.
